Significance of scale-averaged wavelet power (Torrence and Compo, section 4d)

Source: R/wavelet_band_significance.R
wavelet_band_significance.Rd

Averages the wavelet power over a band of periods (a "scale-averaged wavelet power" time series, eq. 24 of Torrence and Compo, 1998) and tests it against a white or AR(1) red noise background. This is the test to use when one asks "is there significant power in this Milankovitch band at this depth?" without looking at every scale separately: the band average is much less noisy than the power at one scale.

Usage

wavelet_band_significance(
  object,
  period_range,
  background = c("ar1", "white"),
  siglvl = 0.95,
  method = c("exact", "torrence"),
  lag1 = NULL,
  delta_j0 = NULL,
  genplot = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'wr_band_significance'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

object

Wavelet to test (list of class analyze.wavelet), the output of analyse_wavelet (Morlet wavelet; its omega_nr, dj, dt, Scale, Power and y are used). Required, no default.

period_range

Band of periods to average (numeric vector of length 2, c(lowest, highest), in the units of the depth/time axis; at least one scale of the wavelet must fall inside), for example c(0.3, 0.5) for an obliquity band. Required, no default.

background

Noise background of the null hypothesis (character, one of "ar1", "white"): "ar1" red noise with the lag-1 autocorrelation lag1, "white" white noise (lag1 is then set to 0). Default="ar1".

siglvl

Significance level of the test (numeric, between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.95 for the 95% level). Default=0.95.

method

How the null distribution of the band average is computed (character, one of "exact", "torrence"): "exact" the weighted sum of exponential variables with a three-moment gamma fit, "torrence" the scaled chi-square distribution of Torrence and Compo (1998, eq. 28); see Details. Default="exact".

lag1

Lag-1 autocorrelation of the AR(1) background (numeric, between 0 and 1). NULL estimates it from the record as in wavelet_significance (mean of the lag-1 autocorrelation and the square root of the lag-2 autocorrelation). Ignored for background = "white". Default=NULL.

delta_j0

Decorrelation length of the scales, only used by method = "torrence" (numeric, > 0); NULL uses 0.6 * 6 / omega_nr, the value 0.6 of Torrence and Compo for omega_nr = 6 rescaled to the omega_nr of object. Default=NULL.

genplot

Plot the band-averaged power with the significance level (logical, TRUE or FALSE), using the plot method. Default=FALSE.

x

Result of wavelet_band_significance (object of class wr_band_significance) to plot. Required, no default.

...

Further graphical arguments passed to plot (e.g. xlim, las; not xlab, ylab, ylim or main, which are set by the method).

Value

An object of class wr_band_significance, a list with: x (depth/time axis), power (the scale-averaged power, in units of variance when the record is standardised), crit (significance level of the band average), pvalue, significant (logical, only points outside the cone of influence), valid, dof (equivalent chi-square degrees of freedom), background_mean (expected band average under the null), period_range, n_scales, lag1, Cdelta, delta_j0, method, background, siglvl. There are print and plot methods.

Details

Two ways of obtaining the null distribution are offered. Both are analytic and run instantaneously.

method = "exact"

(default) The scale-average of the squared modulus of a linear transform of a Gaussian process is a weighted sum of independent exponential variables. The weights are the eigenvalues of a small (number of scales x number of scales) matrix that is computed from the wavelet and the background spectrum with the same Gaussian integrals that define the Morlet wavelet. This is exact for any omega_nr, any dj, any band and any background spectrum, and it needs no tabulated constants. The distribution of the weighted sum is approximated by a three-moment (shifted gamma) fit, which was checked against Monte Carlo simulations with the package's own analyse_wavelet (see the package tests).

method = "torrence"

The published closed form: the band average is a scaled chi-square variable with \(\nu = 2 n_a (S_{avg}/S_{mid}) \sqrt{1 + (n_a \delta j / \delta j_0)^2}\) degrees of freedom (eq. 28), where \(n_a\) is the number of scales, \(S_{avg}\) the harmonic-type mean scale and \(S_{mid}\) the geometric mid-scale of the band, and \(\delta j_0\) an empirical decorrelation length. Torrence and Compo only tabulated \(\delta j_0 = 0.60\) for a Morlet wavelet with omega_nr = 6. Because the Morlet wavelet becomes narrower in log-scale when omega_nr increases, that constant under-estimates the degrees of freedom for larger values, so the test becomes too conservative (at omega_nr = 10 only about 2% instead of 5% of white noise points exceed the 95% level). Here the default is rescaled as \(\delta j_0 = 0.60 \cdot 6 / \omega_0\), with \(\omega_0\) the value of omega_nr,, which was fitted against the exact method for omega_nr between 4 and 12 and is within about 10% of the exact degrees of freedom for bands wider than one octave. Use method = "exact" when the exact answer matters.

Only points whose whole period band lies outside the cone of influence are tested.

The band average is \(\delta j \delta t / C_\delta \sum_j |W_j|^2 / s_j\) (eq. 24). The factor \(C_\delta\) is evaluated numerically for the omega_nr and dj of the object, normalised so that the average over all scales of unit-variance white noise is 1. It only sets the units of power; the significance decision does not depend on it.

The test is for a single point in depth. The band average is strongly autocorrelated along depth, so the number of significant points expected by chance is 5% of the points, but they occur in runs.

References

Torrence, C., Compo, G.P., 1998. A practical guide to wavelet analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 79, 61-78.

See also

wavelet_significance

Examples

set.seed(1)
z <- seq(0, 60, by = 0.1)
d <- data.frame(z, sin(2 * pi * z / 4) + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), length(z))))
wt <- analyse_wavelet(d, dj = 1 / 10, lowerPeriod = 0.4, upperPeriod = 30,
                       verbose = FALSE, omega_nr = 8)
bs <- wavelet_band_significance(wt, period_range = c(3, 5))
bs
#> Significance of scale-averaged wavelet power (exact, ar1 background, level 0.95)
#>   band: periods 3.2 to 4.85 (7 scales)
#>   equivalent degrees of freedom: 3.84 
#>   expected band average under the null: 0.1003   critical value: 0.243 
#>   significant points: 429 of 513 outside the cone of influence
